messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Emma Green <emma@clearview-analytics.com>, procurement@clearview-analytics.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 09 May 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: May forecast gap & churn containment plan — Clearview Analytics

Emma — following up from last week's renewal signal. Finance flagged a forecast gap for Clearview in May: your account is showing a 40% drop in committed ARR vs. plan as of the weekly export. We pulled a short package attached (Clearview_MA_plan_v2.xlsx + audit snapshot) that shows the committed vs. expected cadence and the items we need to reconcile.

Quick summary / asks:
- There's a one-quarter billing enrollment that wasn't captured in HubSpot (line item 3 in the spreadsheet). Can your procurement team confirm PO/contract amendment status?
- We saw usage credits applied that reduced the committed ARR — can you confirm whether those were intended as permanent credits or one-time adjustments?
- If you expect a later ramp (Q3), let us know so we don't over-apply churn probability in the forecast.

Proposed short plan (30/60/90):
1) Today — procurement confirms PO status and flags any contract changes.
2) 48 hours — Redwood to freeze forecast probability pending doc review and produce a revised MR (mutual action plan).
3) 7 days — finalize amendment (DocuSign) or roll back temporary credits and re-sync billing.

If useful, Ben can walk through the usage/credit line items in a 20-minute call today. I've attached the audit snapshot for your procurement and Ben's readout will be useful for internal reconciliation.

Thanks — want to close this into the May book by EOD Tuesday.

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Lead, Renewals
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0172

Marissa — thanks for the quick note and for the attached workbook. A couple of clarifications from our side: we did request a temporary usage credit last month while a data pipeline issue was investigated; that was intended as a one-time adjustment and should not affect our committed ARR. Procurement is also confirming the PO amendment status; I put them on cc.

Two asks back:
- Can Ben share a short line-by-line explanation of the credit adjustment? It will help procurement close the loop.
- We have a mid-June feature delivery that will likely change usage patterns; if we can mark this as a known ramp in your MR, that would be ideal.

I can make time for a 20-minute call this afternoon at 3pm PT if that works for your team.

Best,
Emma
Director, Cloud Operations
Clearview Analytics
emma@clearview-analytics.com

Emma — I can do 3pm PT. Quick context on the credit: the engineering team issued an operational credit covering 2 weeks of excess token consumption during the pipeline incident; the credit was back-dated but intended as non-recurring. I've attached a short export (included in the audit PDF) showing the credit line and how it adjusted billing. On the call I can run through the spreadsheet and point to the exact rows (line 7–9).

Action items for the call:
- Marissa: confirm the revised MR template to include the June feature ramp as a conditional ramp.
- Naomi: prepare a forecast delta (probability and ARR) if credits are reverted vs maintained.
- David: flag any billing-side holdbacks that would delay recognition.

See you at 3pm.

--

Thanks all — good progress. Follow-up notes and agreed next steps: 
1) Procurement will circulate final PO amendment by 5/14 (Marissa will update HubSpot on receipt).
2) Ben to share the 1-page credit breakdown and confirm it's one-time (attachment: Clearview_MA_plan_v2.xlsx, row refs in the audit PDF).
3) Naomi to publish a provisional forecast update by EOD Monday that keeps the account in "conditional commit" (probability 60%) pending PO. She will include separate lines for the two scenarios (credit reversed vs credit kept).
4) If PO completes by 5/14 and the DocuSign link is executed, finance will recognize the committed ARR for May. Otherwise we will de-risk the forecast on the next run.

I will update the deal in HubSpot and mark this as a short-term containment plan; tagging internal play: CHURN-CONTAIN-05.

Thanks again — we should be able to close this into the May forecast if procurement keeps cadence.
